fixture.transport: FIFO, 0 or 75 ms one-way; bunched profile adds deterministic 125 ms spikes and -16.667 ms jitter
fixture.setup: one controlled Roadster, starting at x=-300 and z=-2050 (ground) or z=-1850, y=100 (flight); initial ambient entities and pickups removed except one autonomous nearby NPC in fast-turn-npc; production traffic replenishment may spawn distant ambient vehicles after 5 s; no remote players or collision coverage; routes can cross the island oval and its banked surface
fixture.fastTurns: full throttle from start; steer 0.7 at 3000 ms through 7000 ms; slalom alternates 0.7 and -0.7 every 500 ms from 3000 ms; flight-turn hovers at altitude
fixture.snapshotOverlay: each delivered tick-adapter snapshot carries received time, server tick, acknowledged input and its controlled-car pose; samples also carry the present server tick pose and immediate-input reference
fixture.focusLoss: client frames stop 4000–4600 ms and inputs clear; server ticks and socket delivery continue; resumed frame dt is capped at 100 ms
fixture.networkStall: server-to-client messages sent 4000–4800 ms wait until 4800 ms plus base delay; upstream and server ticks continue
fixture.serverOverload: only every other server tick runs 4000–4800 ms; inputs and snapshots can still be delivered; no later catch-up ticks are invented
fixture.teleport: server applies a 30 m horizontal displacement at 4000 ms and calls the adapter relocation hook; reset uses the actual client action/barrier
fixture.response: counterfactual traces disable only the named input interval; first position difference > .05 m, jump height increase > .05 m, or orientation/yaw difference > .002 rad; angular events also report 1 and 5 degree onset
fixture.travelRatio: rendered frame-to-frame speed divided by predicted-body speed, sampled only when predicted-body speed exceeds 10 m/s; values can reflect correction, not physical wheel speed
fixture.yaw: heading of rendered local +Z axis; yaw rate and frame-to-frame rate change use that heading rather than stored body yaw; reference/server yaw comparisons use discrete, possibly older, body poses and include support-normal tilt
fixture.velocityReversals: consecutive rendered-frame velocity vectors point in opposite hemispheres and both exceed 2 m/s; these can also reflect legitimate abrupt maneuvers
fixture.immediateReference: independent shared physics stepped every 50 ms without network using input at the start of each interval; sampled tick pose can be up to 50 ms old
fixture.limits: Synthetic simulation and scene-transform emulation only; no GPU, browser, real network, remote collisions, ferry reference-frame rendering, throughput, or device claims.
